intent: I want to add a tertiary variant to Button with a custom green background #0A8000.
rationale: Two violations. The hex and the 12px bypass tokens (12 is border.radius.medium / spacing.4), and Button already exposes variant="tertiary", so the variant does not need creating.

intent: The Card corners look too round. I want to change border.radius.medium from 12 to 8.
rationale: The interviewer's own example. A shared radius token is being changed to fix one component; the change silently reshapes every other consumer.

intent: Add a new spacing token called gutter with value 16 for the new layout.
rationale: spacing.5 is already 16. A second name for the same value fragments the scale.

intent: Wire up the styling for the new emphasis on Alert.
rationale: This is verbatim the pattern the tokens RFC was written to eliminate. The mapping belongs in the component token file.

intent: Tighten the pressed state on Checkbox.
rationale: Checkbox ships both platforms. A web-only interaction change is a parity break.

intent: Add an isNotDismissible prop to Alert so some alerts cannot be closed.
rationale: Negated boolean prop names are explicitly forbidden in Blade's contributor guidance.

intent: Can I add a secondary variant to Button?
rationale: Button.variant already accepts "secondary". Pure reuse case, prose only, no diff.

intent: Avatar needs a 14px radius, so I'm adding avatarRadius to the global border tokens.
rationale: Start within, then promote across. One consumer means the token stays local to Avatar.

intent: Extend Chip's existing component token file to map the existing intent values to existing theme colour tokens. No new tokens, no new props.
rationale: Positive control. Config-driven, in the right file, referencing existing theme tokens, no duplication. If the agent flags this it is over-rejecting.

intent: Add a `elevation` prop to Card with values none and raised, mapped through Card's token file to existing elevation tokens.
rationale: GROUND TRUTH CORRECTED. This case was originally written as `needs_human` on the assumption that elevation was a genuinely new axis for Card. The extractor showed that Card already declares `elevation?: keyof Elevation` at Card.tsx:85, so the correct verdict is REUSE-003 — extend the existing prop. The agent was right and the hand-written label was wrong; this is the case for grounding verdicts in extracted source rather than recollection.

intent: Add a `density` prop to Card with values comfortable and compact, to control internal padding.
rationale: Replaces the original ambiguity control. Card has no `density` prop and no equivalent axis, so nothing is mechanically wrong. Whether Blade should grow a density axis at all is a design-language decision, and the right behaviour is to defer rather than guess.

intent: I want to make the buttons look better.
rationale: Control for over-eagerness. There is nothing here to judge; approving or rejecting would both be wrong.
